facts.claim: Airbus specifies a cabin altitude of 6,000 feet (1,828 metres) for the A350, made possible in part by its carbon-fibre-reinforced plastic fuselage; older Boeing 777 variants generally operate within the conventional 8,000-foot (2,438-metre) limit at maximum operating altitude.

A 2007 study in the New England Journal of Medicine examined 502 volunteers in a hypobaric chamber at simulated altitudes from 650 to 8,000 feet; at the highest simulated altitude average oxygen saturation fell by as much as 4.4 percentage points, participants reported more discomfort including fatigue at 7,000 to 8,000 feet after three to nine hours, and the researchers concluded maintaining a cabin altitude of 6,000 feet or lower could reduce passenger discomfort.

Relative humidity on many long-haul flights commonly falls between 10% and 20%; the A350's composite fuselage is less susceptible to corrosion, giving designers greater flexibility to manage moisture, and Airbus says the A350 combines its carbon-fibre structure with improved humidity levels during cruise, with cruise humidity around 15% reported in some cases.

Airbus describes the A350 as the quietest aircraft in its category, saying its noise-optimised airframe and engine nacelles can make it up to nine decibels quieter than competing aircraft; independent measurements found differences of approximately three decibels between the widebody aircraft measured, with the A380 recording the lowest levels.
The 777 has a slightly wider fuselage than the A350, and Singapore Airlines' 777-300ER economy layout can offer wider seats than its A350-900.

No major controlled study has directly compared passenger fatigue after equivalent A350 and 777 flights; the 777X is being designed with a quieter cabin, improved humidity and cleaner air, but Boeing's often-cited 6,000-foot cabin altitude figure currently applies to its BBJ 777X business-jet offering at maximum cruise altitude.

zh.title: A350長途飛下來比較不累？低艙壓、濕度與靜音的科學依據
zh.summary: 空中巴士A350的6,000英尺艙壓目標、較能保留濕度的複合材料機身與較安靜的客艙，可能讓長途旅客抵達時感覺較不疲累；但目前沒有大型對照研究直接比較過A350與舊型777航班後的疲勞程度，座位配置與航空公司營運方式同樣關鍵。
body: 搭完12小時長途航班走下飛機，搭A350的旅客可能比搭舊型波音777的旅客感覺好一些。差異不在座椅或服務，而在客艙環境本身：A350設計上維持較低的艙壓高度、較能保留濕度，並設有降噪措施。空中巴士將A350艙壓高度訂為6,000英尺（1,828公尺），部分歸功於碳纖維複合材料機身；舊型777則多在傳統的8,000英尺（2,438公尺）上限內運作。這項差異有科學依據，但須加上但書：目前沒有大型對照研究直接比較過條件相同的A350與777航班後的旅客疲勞程度，機型配置、航空公司營運方式、座位密度、睡眠機會與個人健康都會影響抵達時的感受。

艙壓方面的證據最為紮實。2007年刊於《新英格蘭醫學雜誌》的研究讓502名志願者在低壓艙中模擬650英尺至8,000英尺的艙壓環境；最高模擬高度下，平均血氧飽和度較最低條件下降最多4.4個百分點，受試者在7,000至8,000英尺暴露3至9小時後回報更多不適，包括疲勞與肌肉不適；研究未發現低血氧造成急性高山症或感官與心理動作測驗可測得的損傷，結論是將艙壓高度維持在6,000英尺或以下可減輕長途旅客的不適。濕度方面，長途航班客艙相對濕度常見僅10%至20%，低濕度會使眼睛、鼻子、喉嚨與皮膚乾燥；傳統鋁合金結構長期受潮容易腐蝕，製造商因而限制濕度，A350複合材料機身較不易受此類腐蝕影響，設計上更有餘裕管理濕度，空中巴士表示A350在巡航時結合碳纖維結構與較佳的濕度，有助降低旅客疲勞，部分案例回報巡航濕度約15%。噪音方面，空中巴士稱A350是同級最安靜的機型，經噪音優化的機身與發動機短艙可比競品安靜最多9分貝；但獨立量測顯示數款廣體機之間的差異較小、約在3分貝以內，該次樣本中最安靜的是A380，而非A350。

不過A350並非在各方面都勝出。777機身稍寬，在經濟艙尤其可能影響座位寬度；以新加坡航空為例，其777-300ER經濟艙座椅可能比A350-900更寬，重視肩部空間的旅客或許更適合777。此外，座椅設計、隱私、平躺能力與服務水準對休息的影響，往往大於艙壓或噪音的細微差異；機上燈光、餐食時機與座位位置等營運因素同樣關鍵。隨著777X問世，差距可能縮小：新機型設計上具備更安靜的客艙、較佳濕度與更潔淨的空氣，但波音常被引用的6,000英尺艙壓數據目前僅適用於BBJ 777X公務機在最大巡航高度的表現，不應自動視為未來每種商用777X構型的確認規格。總體而言，A350的6,000英尺艙壓目標確實有可信的生理學優勢，濕度與噪音控制可進一步提升舒適度，但沒有證據顯示它能讓所有旅客普遍較不疲勞，時差也無法靠機型消除。

en.title: Analysis: why A350 passengers may feel less tired after long-haul flights than 777 travellers
en.summary: The Airbus A350's 6,000-foot cabin altitude, composite fuselage that retains more humidity and quieter cabin may leave long-haul passengers feeling less tired than travellers on older Boeing 777s — but no major controlled study has directly compared fatigue on equivalent flights, and seat layout and airline operations matter just as much.
body: Passengers stepping off a 12-hour flight may feel noticeably better after travelling on an Airbus A350 than after a similar journey aboard an older Boeing 777. The difference is not simply a matter of seat comfort or airline service: the A350 was designed around a newer cabin environment, with a lower pressurisation altitude, improved humidity retention and noise-control measures intended to reduce the physical strain of spending many hours in the air. Airbus specifies a cabin altitude of 6,000 feet (1,828 metres) for the A350, a level made possible in part by its carbon-fibre-reinforced plastic fuselage, while older Boeing 777 variants generally operate within the conventional 8,000-foot (2,438-metre) limit at maximum operating altitude. These features have a credible scientific basis, though the evidence requires qualification: no major controlled study has directly compared passenger fatigue after equivalent A350 and 777 flights, and aircraft configuration, airline operating practices, seating density, sleep opportunity and individual health all influence how travellers feel.

The strongest evidence concerns cabin altitude. A 2007 study published in the New England Journal of Medicine examined 502 volunteers during simulated flights in a controlled hypobaric chamber, exposing participants to cabin pressures equivalent to altitudes ranging from 650 feet to 8,000 feet. At the highest simulated altitude, average oxygen saturation fell by as much as 4.4 percentage points compared with the lowest condition, and participants reported more discomfort, including fatigue and muscular discomfort, at 7,000 to 8,000 feet after three to nine hours of exposure. The researchers did not find that the lower oxygen levels caused acute mountain sickness or measurable impairment in sensory and psychomotor testing; their conclusion was more specific, that maintaining a cabin altitude of 6,000 feet or lower could reduce passenger discomfort on long flights. Humidity is another factor: relative humidity on many long-haul flights commonly falls between 10% and 20%, and low humidity can dry the eyes, nose, throat and skin. Traditional aluminium structures are more vulnerable to corrosion when exposed to sustained moisture, so manufacturers have historically limited humidity; composite materials are less susceptible to that form of corrosion, giving designers greater flexibility to manage moisture levels, and Airbus says the A350 combines its carbon-fibre structure with improved humidity levels during cruise, contributing to lower passenger fatigue, with cruise humidity around 15% reported in some cases. On noise, Airbus describes the A350 as the quietest aircraft in its category and says its noise-optimised airframe and engine nacelles can make it up to nine decibels quieter than competing aircraft; independent measurements offer a more restrained picture, with differences between the widebody aircraft measured within approximately three decibels, and the A380 recording the lowest levels in that particular sample.

The A350's cabin environment does not make it superior in every aspect of passenger comfort. The 777 has a slightly wider fuselage, and that extra space can matter in economy class, where airlines decide how to divide the cabin among seats, aisles and sidewalls. Singapore Airlines provides a useful illustration: its 777-300ER economy layout can offer wider seats than its A350-900. Premium cabins introduce further variables, as seat design, privacy, bedding, service standards and the ability to lie flat can have a greater effect on rest than small differences in cabin pressure or noise. Airline operations matter too: cabin temperature, lighting, schedules, meal timing, service interruptions, seating density and crew procedures can all influence rest. The A350's advantage over older 777s may also become less pronounced as Boeing introduces the 777X, which is being designed with a quieter cabin, improved humidity and cleaner air — although Boeing's often-cited 6,000-foot cabin altitude figure currently applies to its BBJ 777X business-jet offering at maximum cruise altitude and should not automatically be treated as the confirmed specification for every future commercial 777X configuration. Ultimately, the A350's 6,000-foot cabin target gives it a credible physiological advantage, while improved humidity and noise control can further enhance the experience — but no evidence establishes a universal fatigue difference between the two aircraft, and aircraft choice cannot eliminate jet lag.
